A CAPTCHA you can inspect

This is a self-made image challenge, with trained circuit inference and exact Grover evolution simulated on your device. We score every region to compile the oracle. The experiment shows how learned recognition and interference work together; it does not establish faster image detection.

02 / UNDER THE HOOD

A learned eye.
A quantum search.

Recognition and search solve different problems. The interesting part is the boundary between them.

I

The QNN learns a predicate

Each patch becomes eight pixel features. Rotations encode them on four qubits. Trainable rotations and entangling gates shape a measured expectation into a bus score.

pbus(x) = σ(w · ⟨O⟩θ,x + b)

A variational quantum classifier, evaluated with a classical statevector simulator. Separate models train on illustrated vehicle patches and controlled photograph composites.

Variational classifiers ↗
II

The oracle changes phase

Threshold the model’s scores to form a fixed set of marked regions. Put the search register in equal superposition, then flip the sign of each marked amplitude.

Of|i⟩ = (−1)f(i)|i⟩

Here the learned decisions are compiled into a diagonal oracle. The QNN is not executed coherently inside the Grover register.

Grover’s original search algorithm ↗
III

Diffusion amplifies the answer

Reflect the amplitudes about their mean. Repeating the oracle and reflection rotates the state toward marked regions. Measurement samples the final distribution.

Psuccess(k) = sin²((2k + 1)θ)
sin²θ = M/N

For one marked region among 64, six rounds give about 99.66% success with an ideal oracle. More rounds can reduce that probability.

Tight bounds and unknown targets ↗
COUNT THE RIGHT THING

Fewer oracle queries.
There is still a cost to seeing.

Classical unstructured search needs O(N/M) predicate queries. Grover needs O(√(N/M)). Image loading, feature extraction, model evaluation, and constructing a coherent oracle can dominate a real system.

Classical search

Where the experiment ends

The checkpoints store 40 fitted slots. Four final RZ phase angles do not affect the current Z-product readouts; 36 slots remain prediction-influencing. This is not a claim that all 36 are independent. Inspect the parameter audit ↓

The illustrated model uses generated vehicle artwork. The street model uses a photographed bus cutout composited into street crops; testing new placements of that asset does not demonstrate recognition of unseen buses.

The model can miss fragments or amplify false positives. The optimal round count uses the number of marked regions found during compilation; an unknown target count needs a different schedule.

Classifier qubits and search qubits are separate simulated registers. No hardware speedup or real-world detection benchmark is claimed.
